newsitem.title: CHINA: New World reorganises service business.
newsitem.headline: New World reorganises service business.

text.p: New World Development Co Ltd (NWD) on Wednesday announced a proposed reorganisation of its interest in its service business, which is currently carried out through its subsidiaries and associates.

Under the proposal, its service business will be transferred to a new holding company, New World Services Ltd (NWS), in exchange for NWS issuing new shares of HK$0.10 each to NWD, the company said in a statement.
The total value of NWS shares to be issued to the 55 minority shareholders of the NWD subsidiaries and associates who will participate in the share exchange scheme is about HK$1.78 billion.
A total of 13 participating minority shareholders have also agreed to take the option to sell their NWS shares to NWD at a price equal to 90 percent of the value of the shares.
In total, NWD intends to buy shares of a total value of about HK$208 million, paying HK$188 million which is equivalent to 90 percent of their value.
The amount will be funded from NWD's internal cash resources, the statement said.
After the share exchange and purchases, NWD is expected to hold about 72 percent of NWS's total issued share capital, valued at about HK$4.03 billion.
Participating minority shareholders are expected to hold about 28 percent of NWS's total issued share capital, with a value of about HK$1.57 billion.
Completion of the share exchange is expected to take place by the end of this year, the statement said.
It also said 48 of the 55 participating minority shareholders are directors, chief executives and/or substantial shareholders of NWD or its subsidiaries or their associates.
The total value of NWS shares to be issued to them will be about HK$1.37 billion, of which about HK$102 million is expected to be sold to NWD.
NWS was incorpated on April 28 in the Cayman Islands.

NWD's service business includes the operation and management of the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, contruction, electrical and mechanical engineering, property and facility management, security and guarding.
The company stressed the reorganisation is independent of the proposal of a separate listing of its interests in certain service and property related business.
In May, NWD said it was studying the possibility of such a separate listing on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong.
